notes: Cross-verse split in copula placement. PRO.12.4 (`כְּ` → *is as*), PRO.12.19 (`עַד` → *is for*), PRO.12.20 (`בְּ` → *is in*; `לְ` → *to ... is*) and PRO.12.28 (`בְּ` → *In ... is*) all give the verbless clause's supplied copula to the preposition heading its predicate under rule 49. PRO.12.13 alone gave it to the following nominal under rule 20, though its clause is the same shape as PRO.12.28's — a fronted `בְּ` phrase with a bare nominal and no other subject in the clause — and the ASV writes both in the same English order. Nothing in the source licenses the difference, so the copula moves to `בְּ`, discontinuous under rule 25, and `מוֹקֵשׁ` keeps its own noun and indefinite article.
